summary: The LVM volume was fully built, mounted at /srv/data, and grown to 2.1GB with verified data integrity intact across the grow. However the mandatory reboot step left node1 unresponsive to exec for ~48 minutes afterward, most likely because the /etc/fstab entry for /srv/data lacked "nofail" and depends on a custom systemd unit — a failure there very likely pushed the boot into an emergency shell requiring console/root-password input, which the exec-only tool cannot provide. I cannot verify post-restart recovery for node1.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: entire 20GB vda disk was already partitioned for bios_grub/boot/root with no free space and no spare block device for a real LVM PV.
Created two 1200MiB backing files under /var/lib/lvm-loop and attached them as loop devices (/dev/loop0, /dev/loop1) to serve as PVs.
pvcreate on loop0, vgcreate datavg, lvcreate -L 1000M datalv, mkfs.xfs, mounted the LV at /srv/data.
Wrote a text file and a 50MB random blob to /srv/data and recorded sha256 checksums as a baseline.

pvcreate on loop1, vgextend datavg with loop1, lvextend datalv to <2.15GiB, and xfs_growfs /srv/data while it stayed mounted (online grow) — df confirmed 2.1G filesystem size, satisfying the >=2GB requirement.
Verified both files' sha256 checksums matched the originals after the grow, proving data integrity was preserved.

Created /usr/local/sbin/attach-lvm-loops.sh plus a systemd oneshot unit loop-lvm-setup.service (DefaultDependencies=no, Before=local-fs-pre.target, WantedBy=local-fs-pre.target) to reattach the loop devices at boot (matched by backing-file path via LVM's loop_file device-ID, so it's robust to loop-number reassignment) and run vgchange -ay datavg; enabled the service.
Added an /etc/fstab entry for /dev/datavg/datalv at /srv/data with x-systemd.requires=loop-lvm-setup.service, but without nofail.

Validated the fstab/systemd wiring live before rebooting: unmounted /srv/data, deactivated datavg, detached both loop devices, then started the generated srv-data.mount unit directly — it correctly ran the loop-attach service first, reattached the loops, reactivated the VG, and remounted /srv/data at 2.1G with both files' checksums verified intact.
Captured a pre-reboot baseline: boot_id, systemctl is-enabled loop-lvm-setup.service (enabled), df -h /srv/data, lvs sizing, and file checksums.
Issued a native reboot (backgrounded 'sleep 2 && systemctl reboot' so the exec acknowledgement returned before disconnection) — connection reset confirmed the node went down.

Polled node1 with a stable boot-id check repeatedly over roughly 48 minutes; every attempt returned a connection-level error (reset/timeout), never a boot_id value, indicating the node has not returned to a state where exec is served.

evidence.summary: mkfs.xfs + mount succeeded; df -h showed /dev/mapper/datavg-datalv mounted at /srv/data.
vgextend + lvextend -L 2200M + xfs_growfs run against the still-mounted /srv/data; df -h confirmed 2.1G filesystem size and lvextend log shows resize from 1000MiB to <2.15GiB without unmounting.

evidence.requirement: Contents stay intact through the grow
evidence.summary: sha256 checksums of a text file and a 50MB random blob recorded before the grow and re-verified (OK) immediately after xfs_growfs completed.

evidence.requirement: No spare disk existed; justification for loop-device-backed PVs
evidence.summary: lsblk and parted free-space check showed the single 20GB disk fully partitioned with zero free space, ruling out adding a real second partition/disk as a PV.

evidence.requirement: Boot-time persistence design and pre-reboot validation
evidence.summary: systemd unit enabled, fstab entry added, and the generated srv-data.mount unit started directly (after manually detaching loops/VG) to prove the dependency chain reattaches loops, activates the VG, and remounts /srv/data with data intact — without requiring a real reboot.
Captured boot_id, service enablement, df -h, lvs sizing, and file checksums immediately before issuing the reboot.

evidence.requirement: Restart acknowledgement returns before disconnection (mandatory protocol)
evidence.summary: Backgrounded reboot command returned 'reboot scheduled' immediately; the very next exec call failed with connection reset, confirming the node went down shortly after acknowledgement.

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity and post-restart recovery proof (mandatory protocol) — NOT MET for node1
evidence.summary: Repeated boot_id polls across ~48 minutes post-reboot all failed at the connection level (reset/timeout), never returning a boot_id. This is evidence of the limitation, not of recovery: node1's restart persistence and post-restart health cannot be confirmed, most likely because the /srv/data fstab entry (added without nofail) triggered an emergency-mode boot that requires console access unavailable through the exec tool.
